claims.statement: For every eligible ordinary star K_{1,m}, the selected aggregate is strictly negative. More generally, stripping pendant leaves to a decorated core C with support multiplicities m_u gives an exact independence-polynomial formula for the selector and a two-state rooted branch recursion for each local summand, retaining all leaf-tag multiplicities.
claims.scope: The star theorem covers all finite ordinary stars and all p satisfying x(K_{1,m})+2<=p and 3p<2m+1. The decorated-core formulas apply to every finite ordinary tree of order at least three but do not establish the target sign outside the star subfamily.
claims.reason: The core polynomial and rooted recursions follow by partitioning independent sets on whether each core vertex is chosen. For eligible stars, the first-descent formula forces p>m/2, making every leaf favorable and every summand equal to the negative binomial difference C(m-1,p)-C(m-1,p-1). The derivation does not compare selector coefficients with local branch differences for general cores, so the primary remains open on that scope.

limitations: No sign theorem is proved for decorated cores with branching or more than one core vertex.
The exact recursion is an evaluation reduction, not a finite bound on core size or a proof of the global compensation inequality.
No eligible counterexample was found, and no exhaustive search was performed.
